subject: chemistry
title: Hazard symbols and risk assessment
key_idea: A hazard symbol warns of a danger and shows which precaution is needed. To evaluate risk in a practical, name the hazard, give a precaution that matches it and give the reason, such as use a fume cupboard so the toxic gas is not inhaled.

blocks.text: A hazard symbol on a container warns of the danger of the contents. It also tells people which safe-working precautions to use in the laboratory.

items.meaning: Something that can cause harm, such as a toxic gas or a corrosive acid.
How likely it is that the hazard will cause harm in a particular practical.
Something done to reduce the risk of harm.

rows: Poisonous. It can harm you if breathed in, or if it touches the skin or eyes.
Chlorine gas, ammonia gas, barium chloride
Burns or damages skin and eyes.
Concentrated hydrochloric acid, barium hydroxide, calcium hydroxide
Can irritate the skin or harm health.
Harms living things if it escapes, for example by killing fish.

items: A hazard symbol shows the danger and points to the precaution needed.
Toxic, corrosive, irritant and hazardous to the environment need different precautions.

sections.heading: Risks and precautions in a practical

blocks.text: To evaluate the risk in a practical, name the hazard, then give a precaution that matches it. A good answer also gives the reason.

diagram.alt: Pick a hazard and see the precaution and the reason for it.

options.label: Toxic gas, such as chlorine or ammonia
results: The gas is toxic, so you do not inhale it

options.label: Toxic solid, such as barium chloride
results: Wear gloves, wear goggles, or use a fume cupboard
So it does not contact the skin, so it does not contact the eyes, or so you do not inhale it

options.label: Corrosive acid or alkali
results: The substance is corrosive and burns the skin and eyes

options.label: Hazardous to health, such as calcium chloride
results: To protect the eyes and skin

options.label: Hazardous to the environment
results: Do not pour reactants or products down the drain
The substance is hazardous to the environment

items.text: Name the hazard, such as a toxic gas.
Give one precaution that matches it, such as use a fume cupboard.
Link it to the harm it prevents, such as so you do not inhale the gas.

items: Match the precaution to the hazard. A fume cupboard is for toxic gases and vapours.
Gloves protect the skin. Goggles protect the eyes.
General safety, such as tying hair back, is not a precaution for a particular hazard.
Name a precaution that matches the hazard, then give the reason.
Fume cupboard for toxic gases. Goggles or gloves for corrosive substances.
Do not pour substances that are hazardous to the environment down the drain.

checks.q: Chlorine is toxic. State one safety precaution when using chlorine in the laboratory.
Barium hydroxide is corrosive. Give one precaution and the reason for it.
checks.a: Wear goggles so the substance does not contact the eyes (or wear gloves to protect the skin).

checks.q: Explain why reactants should not be poured down the drain when the substance is hazardous to the environment.
checks.a: The substance is hazardous to the environment, for example it could kill fish.

exam_phrases: because the concentrated hydrochloric acid is corrosive
do not dispose of any reactants / products down the drain
because it is hazardous to the environment
so does not contact the skin
so does not contact the eyes
so you do not inhale it

mistakes.right: Protective or safety clothing and PPE are ignored. Name the item, such as goggles or gloves, and give the reason.

mistakes.wrong: Wear a mask or breathing apparatus when using chlorine.
mistakes.right: Masks and breathing apparatus are ignored for toxic gases. Use a fume cupboard.

mistakes.wrong: Tie hair back and wear a lab coat when using a corrosive substance.
mistakes.right: General lab safety and lab coats are ignored. Wear goggles, gloves or eye protection.

mistakes.wrong: Wear gloves so that you do not inhale the gas.
mistakes.right: The reason must match the precaution, and the second mark depends on the first. Gloves protect the skin. A fume cupboard stops you inhaling the gas.

worked_example.question:
Two compounds of barium are barium sulfide and barium chloride.

Barium chloride is toxic.

Explain one safety precaution that should be taken when using barium chloride.
answer_points: Wear gloves, so that it does not contact the skin.
Or wear goggles, so that it does not contact the eyes.
Or use a fume cupboard, so that you do not inhale it.
worked_example.tip: Give one pair. The second mark depends on the first, and protective clothing alone is ignored.
